29.why: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere; weather happens in the troposphere; the ionosphere is part of the thermosphere; meteors burn up in the mesosphere.

30.why: Dry air is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 0.93% argon and 0.03-0.04% carbon dioxide.

31.why: A hygrometer measures humidity, a thermometer temperature, a barometer air pressure and an anemometer wind speed.

32.why: The tropopause separates troposphere and stratosphere, the stratopause stratosphere and mesosphere, the mesopause mesosphere and thermosphere, and the thermopause the thermosphere (ionosphere) and exosphere.

59.why: Savannas are tropical grasslands, the tundra has permafrost, the taiga is coniferous forest and hot deserts have cacti and other xerophytes.

60.why: In the chain grass → rabbit → snake → eagle, grass is the producer, the rabbit the primary consumer, the snake the secondary consumer and the eagle the tertiary consumer.

61.why: The Sundarbans are mangroves, Central India has tropical deciduous forest, the Amazon basin is tropical evergreen rainforest and Siberia is coniferous taiga.

82.why: The Atlantic is S-shaped, the Pacific is ringed by the Ring of Fire, the Arctic is the smallest ocean and the Indian Ocean is land-locked on its northern side.

84.why: The abyssal plain is the flat deep-sea floor, trenches are the deepest parts, the continental shelf is the shallow edge and the continental slope is the steep drop beyond it.

85.why: Estuaries mix fresh and sea water; the Baltic Sea has low salinity from river inflow; the Dead Sea is extremely salty; the open ocean averages about 35 parts per thousand.

87.why: Folding bends rocks under stress, faulting cracks the crust, volcanism erupts magma and an earthquake is sudden shaking from fault movement.
R: Bending of rocks due to stress
Eruption of magma from beneath the Earth's surface
Sudden shaking due to fault movement

94.why: Block mountains form by faulting, fold mountains by folding, volcanic mountains by eruptions and residual mountains are what remains after erosion.

106.why: Erosion removes surface material, weathering breaks rocks in place, deposition lays sediment down elsewhere and mass wasting moves rock downslope under gravity.
R: Removal of surface material by agents like water or wind
Accumulation of sediments in new locations
Downward movement of rocks due to gravity

113.why: Rivers cut V-shaped valleys, glaciers carve U-shaped valleys, wind deposits sand dunes and rivers build deltas at their mouths.
R: Formed by river deposition at mouth

132.why: Urbanisation is the growth of cities, pollution is contamination of the environment, deforestation is clearing forests and conservation is protecting natural resources.
R: Growth of cities and the migration of people to urban areas.
Contamination of the environment with harmful substances.
Clearing of forests for other land uses.
Protection and preservation of natural resources.

133.why: The biosphere is the zone of life, the atmosphere the envelope of gases, the lithosphere the solid outer layer and the hydrosphere all of Earth's water.
R: Solid outer layer of the Earth.

139.why: The stratosphere holds the ozone layer, the exosphere is the outermost boundary with space and the troposphere is where weather happens.

175.why: Stratus clouds form sheets, nimbus clouds bring rain, cirrus clouds are wispy and feathery and cumulus clouds look like cotton heaps.

176.why: Condensation turns vapour into liquid, transpiration is water loss from plants, evaporation turns liquid into vapour and precipitation is water or snow falling.

178.why: Albedo is reflectivity, saturated air holds the most water vapour it can, the lapse rate is the change of temperature with height and an inversion is warm air lying above cold air.

179.why: Carbon dioxide traps heat (greenhouse effect), ozone absorbs UV rays, oxygen is used in respiration and nitrogen is essential for plant growth.

219.why: Conical conifers suit the taiga, low plants and thick fur suit the tundra, water-storing stems suit deserts and drip-tip leaves suit rainforests.

220.why: Each cycle is named after the substance it moves: N2, O2, CO2 and H2O.

221.why: The deer is a primary consumer, grass a producer, the tiger an apex predator and fungi decomposers.

222.why: Air makes up the atmosphere, living things the biosphere, rocks and soil the lithosphere and water the hydrosphere.

223.why: Tundra is cold and treeless, rainforest hot and wet, taiga has long cold winters and deserts get very little rain.

256.why: Neap tides occur at the quarter moons, when Sun and Moon pull at right angles; spring tides occur at full and new moon, when they line up.

257.stem: Match the Current with its Ocean:
257.why: Kuroshio – Pacific; Gulf Stream – Atlantic; Agulhas – Indian; East Greenland – Arctic.

258.why: Fresh water from rain and rivers lowers salinity; evaporation leaves salt behind and raises it.

259.why: The Puerto Rico Trench is the deepest point of the Atlantic; the Mariana Trench, in the Pacific, is the deepest on Earth.
